Juno unlocks the bakery at 4 AM. The street outside is still dark and wet, and her breath fogs in the cold.

She ties her apron, flicks on the ovens and slides the first tray of croissants in. Tight on her flour-dusted hands.

The bell above the door rings. Theo, her neighbour, leans in, half asleep, holding an empty mug. Juno: You're early. Theo: You're always earlier.

Juno fills his mug without a word. The camera pushes in on the steam curling up between them.

Sunrise. The window glows orange and the whole street smells like butter. Pull back to reveal a queue already forming outside.
